questions.question: Responsive design means a site:

options.text: Adapts layout/content to different screen sizes and devices
Requires a separate mobile domain only

questions.explanation: Responsive design fluidly adapts via fluid grids, flexible media, and media queries — one codebase for all devices.

questions.question: The viewport meta tag <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width"> does:

options.text: Tells mobile browsers to use the device width (not a zoomed-out 980px default)

questions.explanation: Without it, mobile renders at ~980px and scales down. width=device-width makes CSS media queries match the real device width.

questions.question: Mobile-first design means:

options.text: Write base styles for small screens, then enhance for larger via min-width media queries

questions.explanation: Mobile-first: default = mobile styles; min-width queries add layout as the viewport grows. Often improves performance (less override).

questions.question: Fluid typography can use:

options.text: clamp(min, preferred, max) for responsive font sizes

questions.explanation: clamp() gives a fluid size bounded between min and max (e.g. clamp(1rem, 2vw + 1rem, 1.5rem)) — great for responsive type.

questions.question: Relative units like % and fr help responsiveness because they:

options.text: Scale with their container/viewport instead of fixed pixels

questions.explanation: Fluid units (% , vw, fr, em) adapt to context; fixed px does not. This is core to fluid grids.

questions.question: A responsive image strategy includes:
questions.explanation: Serve right-sized images per device via srcset/sizes and art-direction via <picture> to save bandwidth and improve LCP.

questions.question: Common breakpoints are chosen based on:

options.text: Real device/content needs, not just 'phone/tablet/desktop' labels

questions.explanation: Design by where your layout breaks, using content-driven breakpoints — avoid rigid device-class assumptions.

questions.question: Which helps a layout reflow from multi-column to single-column on small screens?

options.text: Flex wrap or Grid auto-fit/minmax with a max-width media query

questions.explanation: Flex wrap or Grid's auto-fit/minmax naturally collapse to fewer columns; media queries can force single-column past a breakpoint.
